fields.description:
## Context

`fixture_selection.select_candidates` groups a criterion's matched findings by `norm_id` and
also compares finding `norm_id` sets across a ticket's successive reviews. On the REAL committed
plan-review corpus these paths raise `KeyError: 'norm_id'`. `select_from_corpus` reconstructs
findings from every `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar event across ALL committed history
(`_review_findings` -> `corpus._load_ticket_events`, keyed by review-event uuid). The `norm_id`
field is emitted by the sidecar `_slim` projection UNCONDITIONALLY — current `_slim`
(`sidecar.py:664`, `"norm_id": norm_id(f)`) writes it for every finding regardless of tier, and
`norm_id()` (`sidecar.py:311-319`) never returns None. That line was ADDED by commit
`314e4191c826` (2026-06-29). Sidecar events committed BEFORE that commit predate the field, so
their reconstructed findings carry no `norm_id` key at all — the crash is a schema-VINTAGE gap in
historical records, NOT current `_slim` tier behavior.

Evidence (scan of the tickets tracker via `_review_findings`, recorded here as the
`[non-codebase]` provenance attestation for this root-cause claim): 1437 of 79914
criterion-naming findings lack a `norm_id` key; ALL 1437 have a review-event timestamp before
2026-06-29 and ZERO are after; they span BOTH tiers (LLM 1299, DET 138). The vintage cutoff
matches commit `314e4191c826` exactly. The first such finding aborts the whole
candidate-selection pass, so the fixture-mining pipeline (epic 65dd-e93b-666a-4caa) cannot run
over real history at all — it blocks ticket 67aa's live admission run (AC10).

A norm-less finding is subscripted `finding["norm_id"]` at SIX sites reached from
`select_candidates`: the `_fire_rows` grouping (`fixture_selection.py:234`) AND — via
`_author_response_norm_ids` -> `classify_finding_survival` — `labels.py:167,169`, plus
`_criterion_sets`/churn `labels.py:184,220,221`. A fix scoped to `_fire_rows` alone would leave
the `classify_finding_survival` path (reached whenever a ticket has two reviews with differing
`material_fingerprint`) still crashing.

## Approach

Normalize norm-less findings out ONCE at the `select_candidates` entry — the single point every
eligible review passes through before ANY norm-keyed consumer. At the top of `select_candidates`,
rebuild each review as `{**review, "findings": [f for f in review["findings"] if
f.get("norm_id") is not None]}`, then proceed unchanged. Because `_eligible_reviews`, `_fire_rows`,
`_no_fire_rows`, and `_author_response_norm_ids` all derive from this list, the single normalization
covers all six subscript sites — and it protects BOTH the public `select_candidates` (direct
callers / tests) and `select_from_corpus` (which calls it).

Rationale for the entry-boundary normalization over scattered per-consumer defensive reads: a
finding with no `norm_id` has no stable cross-review identity, so it cannot participate in ANY
norm-keyed operation (reproduction-consensus grouping, author-response survival, or per-criterion
churn) — excluding it once at the entry is both the minimal single-point fix and semantically
correct. For every norm-BEARING finding the normalized lists are byte-identical to today, so all
existing selection behavior is unchanged. No change to `labels.py` is needed: the boundary keeps
norm-less findings from ever reaching it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `select_candidates` no longer raises `KeyError: 'norm_id'` when an eligible review's findings
      include a criterion-naming finding with no `norm_id` key, exercised through BOTH norm-keyed
      paths: `_fire_rows` grouping AND the `_author_response_norm_ids` -> `classify_finding_survival`
      survival path (two reviews of one ticket with differing `material_fingerprint`, at least one
      norm-less finding) — the run returns rows without error (`pytest`).
- [ ] A finding lacking `norm_id` contributes NO candidate and does not perturb the candidates
      produced by norm-bearing findings for the same criterion: the emitted rows for an eligible
      set containing a norm-less finding equal the rows produced when that finding is absent
      (`pytest`).
- [ ] Existing norm-bearing selection behavior is unchanged: the module's current
      `test_fixture_selection` suite still passes (`pytest`).
- [ ] Selection remains deterministic — two `select_candidates` runs over the same eligible set
      return byte-identical manifest rows (`pytest`).

## Definition of Done

`make lint` / `make typecheck` / targeted `pytest` pass; the fix lands through Gerrit
(`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`); the fixture-mining selection pass runs over the real
corpus without the `norm_id` KeyError.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py` — normalize norm-less findings out at the
  `select_candidates` entry (single point; covers `_fire_rows` + the `classify_finding_survival`
  and churn paths in `labels.py`).
- `tests/unit/test_fixture_selection.py` — held-out regression: a norm-less finding routed
  through both the fire-grouping and the author-response/survival paths.
